$comment: Level three, not five. Madden stands at the mouth of Route 1 with a sight range of four, so he is the first fight nobody can walk past, and stone resists BOTH of Cinderpaw's move types while hitting it back for double. Measured: a level-five Pebblet beat a level-six Cinderpaw in 93 battles out of 100. At level three the Cinderpaw wins about nine times in ten.
name: Madden
intro: Six hours out, six hours back.
Most interesting thing I have seen all day. No offence to the rock.
defeat: Well. That is the second interesting thing.
victory: Ah. Sorry. I did warn you about the rock.
afterward: Still six hours from anywhere.
I did find a rock, though. Genuinely beautiful rock. Nobody will look at it.
Ashgate is north. Stay on the spine road and do not get clever with it.

name: Wray
intro: I am counting pipwings for Professor Sorrell. There are meant to be forty on this route.
There are eleven.
...Battle me, I need to think about something else.
defeat: Eleven. Still eleven.
victory: Sorry. I have been out here a while.
afterward: Twelve now. One came back. That is something.

name: Bex
intro: I have ONE.
Dad says one is plenty until I can look after one.
defeat: That was my one. That is just rude.
victory: ONE! That is all you need!
afterward: When I am eight I get another one.
I have already picked which. It does not know yet.

$comment: Novice, not trained, and level four. He is the second fight on Route 1 and the only Tide on it: against a level-seven Cinderpaw the trained level-five Rillfry won 91 times in 100. Ottel is a man guarding a pond, not a tactician.
name: Ottel
intro: Pond is mine. Fish are mine. Argument is available.
defeat: Fine. Pond is still mine.
victory: Told you. Pond is mine.
afterward: Come back at dusk. Different fish then. Better fish.

name: Cale
intro: Rangers walk this road so nobody else has to worry about it.
Let me see whether I need to worry about you.
defeat: No. I do not need to worry about you at all. Good.
victory: Right. Then I do have to worry about you.
Turn back at Ashgate if it goes badly. That is not failing. That is the job.
afterward: Stay out of the deep grass until that one of yours has some weight on it.
Nothing on this route will kill you. Plenty of it will embarrass you.
And watch the pond at dusk. Only at dusk. Do not ask me why. I have stopped asking.
$comment: Ranger, so he keeps the trained tier -- he is one of the few people on the road whose job is reading a fight. Level 7 down to 5 with the rest of the third pass.

name: Ilm
intro: This is a survey corridor. It is not closed, exactly.
It is just easier for both of us if you go around.
...You are not going around, are you.
defeat: Fine. Walk it. Look at the stakes if you like, they are only stakes.
The Concord is not hiding anything. We are measuring.
victory: Thank you. Genuinely. Go around.
afterward: Every seventy years this coast drowns. We are going to stop that. That is all this is.

name: Rowe
intro: Everyone comes in swinging. Everyone.
Go on then. Swing at me and see how far it gets you.
defeat: That was not swinging. That was thinking. Good.
victory: Swinging. Told you.
afterward: Nettlebug cannot hurt you. It was never trying to.
It was making you slow while I picked the fight I wanted.

name: Pell
intro: Two of mine. Neither of them fast, neither of them frightening.
See how long they last anyway.
defeat: They lasted a while. You lasted longer.
victory: Patience. That is all that was.
afterward: Tove will put something in front of you that you cannot knock over.
When that happens, stop hitting it. Start asking what it is bad at.

$comment: The first Hall in the game, and the one whose stated job is to teach that battling is strategy rather than damage. Bramblehusk is the lesson: 78 Defence, 78 Special Defence, a Brace to raise the first of them, and -- deliberately -- no second attack. You cannot out-hit it at level nine, so the fight is about type, order and patience. Its own offence is one Vinewhip, which is why a player who does not work it out still survives long enough to try again; and it carries flat-zero IVs and no bag item, because the engine never consumes a foe-side item and one Potion in that list is an unlimited heal. MEASURED, and not against the shipped harness: that harness unlocks Slatewing and Gravelet at level ten because level ten used to mean Route 2 had been walked, and Briarbell comes BEFORE Route 2. Against a party a Route 1 player really holds -- the starter plus Nibbet, Tuftail, Pipwing -- this reads 73/87/74 percent at level nine and 96/92/86 at level ten for Sprigling, Cinderpaw and Rilltail. Losable on arrival, comfortable after the two Hands. That is a first wall, not a stopping point.
name: Tove Alder
intro: Tove Alder. I keep the Bell Hall, and before that I kept the hedge, which is the same job.
You will want to knock my last one over. Everybody does.
You will not. Work out what else you have.
defeat: There. That is the whole of it.
You stopped hitting it and started beating it. Those are different things.
victory: It only had to stand there. That should tell you something.
Come back when you have a second idea.
afterward: The bells were hung by people who could not have fought us for an afternoon.
They still put six bells in a tree that outlived them. Think about what that took.

$comment: First trainer on Route 2. Levels 7 and 8 now come down to 5 and 6 with the rest of the third pass. The rule this pass applies everywhere: an ORDINARY trainer stands three or more levels below the player who is raising a team, not the player who never switches. Those are two different people five levels apart by Brackwater, and the first two passes tuned for the average of them, which is nobody.
name: Dell
intro: I am supposed to be cataloguing thorn growth.
It grew across the whole spur in one season. That is the catalogue.
defeat: Fine. Back to the thorn.
victory: Come back when your notes are better than mine.
afterward: That thorn was not there in spring. I have the sketch to prove it.

name: Pike
intro: Uphill both ways, this road.
I have walked it twice today. Give me a reason to stop.
defeat: There. That will do. Sitting down now.
victory: Still uphill. Sorry.
afterward: Stonewake is over the rise. You will smell the quarry before you see it.

name: Juna
intro: Ranger post. I check the ledges, the pond and the thorn.
Two of those are behaving.
defeat: Good. Then you are not the thing out here that is wrong.
victory: Not today. Go back down to Ashgate and let me get on with the thorn.
afterward: If you ever learn to cut that thorn, come and find me. I want to know what is behind it.

name: Shale
intro: Walking down for the week. You are walking up.
One of us has made a mistake.
defeat: Still going down. Cheerfully now.
victory: Then I was right about which of us made the mistake.
afterward: Roxen does not go easy. Roxen has never gone easy in her life.

name: Wren
intro: I do a routine with the slatewings on the quarry face.
Nobody comes. The slatewings come.
defeat: That was a better routine than mine.
victory: Curtain.
afterward: Dusk is the good hour. Come and watch, it is free and it always will be.

name: Corrin
intro: Stones first, then Roxen.
Nobody has ever done it the other way round.
defeat: Stones are yours, then.
victory: Push the stones. Then come back.
afterward: Three plates. Three stones. It is not a riddle, it is just heavy.

name: Wick
intro: You get one thing wrong in a quarry and the quarry corrects it for you.
Same here, roughly.
defeat: Corrected. Go on up.
victory: Try again when the stones are where they belong.
afterward: Verdant and Tide give her trouble. That is not a secret, it is a type chart.

$comment: Chalkmar is a 452-point fully evolved kin and it is the ace of the FIRST Kin Hall. Its level is pinned at 14-18 by tests/content.test.js, so level was never the dial available here -- and two passes of lowering the kin AROUND it never touched the thing that was actually winning her the fight. Measured against a player raising a team, who arrives at Kellowmere at THIRTEEN with a starter that has not evolved yet (all three evolve at 16), Roxen beat a Cinderpaw 100 times out of 100. One move was doing it: stonefling is Stone, which is STAB on a Stone/Iron kin and doubles into Flame, so it landed at three times the weight of anything Chalkmar had. Taking that single move out took Cinderpaw from 0 to 81 percent and touched nothing else. Chalkmar keeps two Stone moves, both defensive -- Bulwark and Grit Field -- plus Gravelspray, so it is now literally the kin her own defeat line describes: something you out-wait rather than out-hit. Flat-zero IVs on top (Hall kin, not hand-picked champions) and the escorts down to 8 and 9. Also removed: her bag Potion. Battle.doItem never consumes a foe-side item, so a single entry in that list is an UNLIMITED 20 HP heal fired at a 70 percent rate every turn she drops below thirty percent. Put it back when the engine consumes it. Measured now, party the size of hers, no items: 100/98/100.
name: Roxen Quill
intro: Roxen Quill. I keep the Stone Hall, and before that I kept the west face for nineteen years.
You moved the stones. Good. That is the whole lesson, really.
Now find out whether you can move me.
defeat: Hah. All right.
You did not out-hit me. You out-waited me. That is the harder one.
victory: Not yet. Go and put some weight on them.
The stones will still be where you left them.
afterward: The quarry road north is shut until the face settles. Do not test me on it.

$comment: Tarin at Stonewake, two weeks and one Bond Crest later. The id names the starter he was GIVEN, not the form he brings. He is BEHIND the player here on purpose: he spent the week being thrown out of the Meridian office instead of fighting the Hallkeeper. His bench is two plain beast kin on purpose as well. Every elemental bench that was tried pulled the three branches apart -- a Slatewing (stone/gale) on its own dropped a Verdant player from 93 percent to nothing, because gale halves verdant while his ace is still weak to it. Beast is neutral to all three starters, so the only type relationship left in the fight is the one that belongs there: his ace loses to yours. Measured at 300 runs with simulate.mjs's rate(starter, level, id, 300, 'novice', 3) -- novice play, no items, three kin: 11/12/94 percent at level 14, 53/49/100 at 15, and 99/97/100 at 16 and up. The cliff at 16 is the starter evolving, not the tuning. Arriving at Stonewake underlevelled is meant to be a real fight; arriving on the curve is a win that still costs a kin.
name: Tarin
intro: Three days in this town and that grey office has thrown me out twice.
The second time they carried me. Politely. That is the part that bothers me.
Come on. I need to hit something I am allowed to hit.
defeat: Fine. FINE. Twice this week I have lost to somebody with a badge on.
Go and take the Crest off her, one of us should have it.
And {name} — ask that office what they want with the quarry cores. Watch their faces.
victory: There. I needed that more than you did, and I am not sorry.
Go and get patched up. I have nowhere better to be thrown out of.
afterward: Do not look at me like that. I am going back in tomorrow.

$comment: Tarin at Stonewake, two weeks and one Bond Crest later. The id names the starter he was GIVEN, not the form he brings. victory: There. I needed that more than you did, and I am not sorry.

afterward: Do not look at me like that. I am going back in tomorrow.

name: Bram
intro: Forty head over that crest this morning and I lost an hour of it standing still.
Waiting on a dray. Then another dray. Then a thing on six wheels with a tarpaulin over it.
defeat: Priority of passage, the notice says. Nobody asked me what my priority was.
victory: Stand at the milestone a while. Count them. See if you get to the same number I do.
afterward: Mossback keeps the herd calm on the incline. Do not ask me how. It sits there and they stop shaking.
Nothing keeps me calm on the incline. I have looked into it.

name: Sill
intro: Professor Sorrell has me counting traffic on this road. Twice a day, same spot, same notebook.
He asked for a season of it. I have four weeks and I have run out of pages.
defeat: Two hundred and six loads. Up. All of them up. None of them have come back down.
victory: Then you have not been reading the numbers either. Nobody reads the numbers.
afterward: It is not the count that bothers me. It is that every one of them is going to the same place.

name: Holt
intro: Forty years on this ridge. I have seen the road busy. Busy is a fair season and a full market.
This is not busy. Busy goes both ways.
defeat: Good. I would rather it was somebody young out here this time.
victory: No. Go away and get older. It is the only training that ever worked on me.
afterward: They are polite. That is what I cannot get past. Every one of them has been polite to me.
Nobody is that polite about stone and rope.
$comment: The ONLY trainer in the game left on the veteran tier, which is the tier that switches out of a bad matchup. That is deliberate: his class is literally Veteran and his opening line is forty years on this road. Everywhere else the third pass moved tiers down to describe the PERSON rather than the position on the map -- hikers, students, anglers, drovers, performers and swimmers all press the biggest number on the screen now, and Rangers, Surveyors, Hall Hands and the rival read the type chart without switching. A novice trainer that switches optimally does not feel novice, it feels like the game cheating.

name: Ivo
intro: You are the one from the Ashgate corridor. Ilm mentioned you.
She said you asked good questions. That was not a compliment, it was a report.
defeat: Fine. Fine.
Go down to the office at Salthollow and ask them yourself. They will tell you more than I can.
Ask why a body with forty stations has stopped collecting from any of them.
victory: Good. Now go around.
afterward: Seven of my stations are on this ridge. The Foundation has put a new box beside four of them.
Better boxes than mine. Warmer, too. Nobody asked me and nobody had to.
$comment: The last Concord trainer in the game, standing at his own obsolete wind station on Eastwind Ridge while the Foundation runs a yard below him. Voltwick was pinned to 14 for three passes and read TWENTY-SEVEN PERCENT against a lone Tide starter, because Spark answers Tide and a 452-BST spark at your own level is not a fight, it is a wall. Down to 13, which is where the rest of the ridge tops out.

name: Teal
intro: Downhill from here all the way to the sea.
That is not a metaphor. I checked.
defeat: Downhill for me too, then.
victory: Rest at Salthollow. Everyone says that. Everyone hates it and everyone does it.
afterward: You can smell the flats from the second ledge. Try it.

name: Gorse
intro: Salt up, stone down. Thirty years, same road, same load, nothing ever changes.
Which is how I know that second post out there used to be underwater.
defeat: Look at the post on your way down. Then tell me nothing changes.
victory: Salt up. Stone down. Nothing changes.
afterward: The flats flooded to that post every spring of my life. Look where the water sits now.

name: Nesh
intro: Cannot swim the channel any more. Water is wrong.
So I stand here instead and battle people. It is less satisfying.
defeat: Wrong water. Wrong everything.
victory: Stay out of the deep. I mean it.
afterward: Used to be a current here you could ride to the pier. It stopped in the spring.

name: Bay
intro: Flats are full. Channel is empty. That has never happened.
defeat: Full flats. Empty channel. Explain that to me.
victory: Ask at the pier. They will tell you the same thing.
afterward: Everything that can leave the deep has come inshore. Everything.

name: Rill
intro: Shallow is walkable. Deep is not. Learn the difference here, not out there.
defeat: Learned it, then.
victory: Read the water before you step in it.
afterward: I went in the deep lane on my first day here. In front of everyone.
That is why I say it twice to everybody. Shallow is a road. Deep is a wall.

name: Cove
intro: Most people rush the middle and end up back at the door.
defeat: Not most people, then.
victory: Back to the door with you.
afterward: The channel to your left is deep the whole way. It is not a shortcut, it is a wall.

name: Skell
intro: Island in the middle. Everyone gets here. Not everyone leaves.
defeat: Go on up. She is waiting and she does not like waiting.
victory: Come back drier.
afterward: Spark and Verdant. That is what she cannot answer. I did not tell you that.

$comment: The wall at the end of the content. Her party carries two fully evolved kin against a player whose starter is mid-stage, which is correct -- she is a Keeper. Third pass: levels 18/19/20/21 down to 16/17/18/19, flat-zero IVs on the Tidewrack, and the hand-written all-attack movesets stripped off the back two so their natural learnsets (which carry status moves) give the player a turn to breathe. Her bag Potion is gone for the same reason Roxen s is -- the engine never consumes a foe-side item, so it was an unlimited heal, not a Potion. Measured with a party the size of hers and no items at all, at the level a team-raiser really walks in with: 88/85/94 percent. She is still the hardest thing in the game and every other trainer now reads above ninety.
name: Mabry Sull
intro: Mabry Sull. Forty years on this channel, twenty-two of them keeping this Hall.
You got across my floor without drowning. That is most of it.
The rest is whether you can stand still while something bigger than you comes in.
defeat: Ha. Good. Genuinely good.
You did not fight the water. You waited for it. That is the whole art.
victory: The sea does not care how fast you are. Come back when you have learned to wait.
afterward: Ask the harbourmaster about the soundings. Then ask why the Concord took them at night.

$comment: Tarin takes the starter the PLAYER'S beats. docs/TARIN.md carries the measurements that decided it; the short version is that the other way round has no fair setting at all. At equal level a rival holding the type advantage wins 71 to 100 percent of the time, and the level-three handicap that used to correct for that turned the fight into a 97 to 100 percent walkover in the other direction. Sorrell hands both of them a level six kin the same morning; Tarin's is one level up because he has been out on the road since before it was light picking fights, which is the only training either of them has done. Rolled IVs, novice play, one kin, no items. Measured at 300 runs with simulate.mjs's rate(starter, 6, id, 300, 'novice') -- pinned to level SIX, because the fight happens the minute the player leaves the lab and the harness's own table samples the Hearthmere stage at its midpoint instead: the player wins 99, 91 and 82 percent leading Sprigling, Cinderpaw and Rilltail. The surviving HP matters as much as the win -- a separate 400-run pass leaves the winner on 60, 55 and 40 percent of full over two and a half to four and a half turns. The scene immediately after this one has the player's mother put the party back together, and that scene is a lie if the fight costs nothing.
name: Tarin
intro: Do not go easy on me. I will be able to tell, and I will bring it up forever.
defeat: Oh. So that is what that feels like.
victory: Ha! I win. I WIN.

name: Tarin
intro: Do not go easy on me. I will be able to tell, and I will bring it up forever.
defeat: Oh. So that is what that feels like.
victory: Ha! I win. I WIN.

name: Corrin
intro: Stones first, then the Keeper.
Nobody has ever done it the other way round and lived to boast.
defeat: Stones are yours, then.
victory: Set the counterweight. Then come back.
afterward: Three plates, three stones, and a fourth stone because somebody always
puts one somewhere daft. That fourth stone has saved this Hall a lot of shouting.

name: Ferro
intro: Down here everything is heavy and everything is slow.
You will notice I said everything.
defeat: ...All right. Not everything.
victory: Slow beats fast underground. Ask anyone who has run down here.
afterward: Twelve years the Hall has had this gallery and it has never once flooded.
Three galleries below us have. The Keeper checks the level herself. Every day.

name: Mattock
intro: Last one before her. That is not a warning, it is a courtesy.
Some people would rather turn round here and nobody thinks less of them.
defeat: Go on, then. She has heard the cage.
victory: Come back down when you have got your wind.
afterward: She sits in that office at sixty fathom because she says a Keeper should be
somewhere real. I have never worked out whether that is wisdom or stubbornness.
Fifteen years down here and I have decided it does not matter which.

$comment: Hall 2, Terra, and the whole party is built to be out-waited rather than out-hit, which is what her own defeat line claims. The type chart is the problem this row exists to solve: Terra is weak to Tide, Verdant and Frost, so Rilltail and Sprigling have an easy answer -- and Terra and Stone BOTH hit Flame for double, so a Cinderpaw player faces a Hall that punishes them for every kin on the field. First measured build (Emberbore 14, Burrowen 16, everything holding Gravelspray) read 83/49/89 on the matched-party row and 49 percent is not a fight, it is a wall. So her offence is almost all BEAST now: Gravelet carries Strike, Quickstep and Brace and no Terra move at all, and the ace is Burrowen at fifteen, which has not learned Gravelspray yet (level 18), so it swings Beast the whole fight -- neutral into Flame. Silthopper is the one kin that still carries Gravelspray, so a Sprigling player cannot walk it with one move. Flat-zero IVs on the ace and no bag item: Battle.doItem never consumes a foe-side item, so one Potion in that list is an unlimited 20 HP heal fired every turn she drops below thirty percent, not a Potion. Put it back when the engine consumes it. Measured, novice play, no items, a party the size of hers at the level a team-raiser really arrives with: 100/95/99 for Sprigling, Cinderpaw and Rilltail.
name: Roxen Quill
intro: Right. Lamps down, and let us find out what you have got.
Terra, weight and patience, and nothing in my hand that hits especially hard.
Nothing in my hand has to.
defeat: Hah. All right.
You did not out-hit me. You out-waited me. That is the harder one.
victory: Not yet. Go up, get your wind, and come back down.
The stones will still be where you left them. So will I.
afterward: Kerb Street east when you are ready. Tideglass is a long way and worth it.
And take a look at the water when you get there. Just look at it.

$comment: ACT 2, the night on the coast road. The first half of the only fight in the game the player did not choose, so it is deliberately not a wall: two kin, no bag items, and an ace four levels UNDER the Keeper the player has just beaten. That is not a mistake -- these are staff with a licence, not Trainers, and the weight of the scene is meant to come from being jumped on a road rather than from a difficulty spike with no clinic in between. Anchorling leads and Lantric closes rather than the other way round: measured with anchorling as the ace the same pair drops a two-kin party to 0-82 percent, because iron/tide at that level is bulky enough that a party which has just fought a Keeper cannot break it. Measured with tests/helpers/simulate.mjs at L19, novice play, no items, matched party: 100 / 96 / 100 percent (sprigling / cinderpaw / rilltail). The lone-starter floor is 47 / 40 / 0 and is the usual one-kin-against-two floor, not a target.
name: Kesh
intro: Nobody is going to be unpleasant about this if nobody makes it necessary.
defeat: Fine. Fine. That is one of us.
victory: Sit down. Somebody will come and find you in the morning.
afterward: I have a licence and a number and neither of them is going to help me now.

$comment: The second half, fought back to back with Kesh and no clinic in between, which the simulator cannot model -- so the single-fight numbers are read as a ceiling and the levels are set under them. The pair totals four kin, the same weight as the Keeper, rather than six. The types are chosen so the two agents punish DIFFERENT branches and cancel out: Kesh carries tide against the flame starter, Ordell carries gale against the verdant one and spark against the tide one, and nobody is singled out. Measured at L19, novice play, no items, matched party: 99 / 100 / 100 percent. If this ever measures under ninety, drop Ordell first -- he is the one being fought on a half-dead party.
name: Ordell
intro: Kesh asked. I am not going to.
defeat: That is not - no. No, that is not what I was told to expect.
victory: Nothing personal in it. There never is, and that is the trouble with us.
afterward: She had no business being out here either. Ask her about that sometime.

$comment: ACT 2, in Tideglass after the night on the road. OPTIONAL -- he asks and the player may say no, which is the cheapest difficulty valve there is, and onLoss is "continue" so losing to him is a scene rather than a whiteout and he offers again. Keyed by the species HE leads with, per docs/TARIN.md, never by the player s. The bench is the two beast kin he has carried since Route 1: neutral to all three starters, which is what keeps the three branches level, and the point of the scene besides -- he has not swapped his team out, he has just worked out what it is for. Measured at L19, novice play, no items, matched party: 95 / 91 / 100 percent (sprigling / cinderpaw / rilltail).
name: Tarin
intro: No talking through it. No jokes. Just come at me.
defeat: Right.
Right, good. That is what I needed to see.
victory: Ha! - no. No, I do not want it like that. Heal up and do it again.
afterward: Fifteen carts, by the way. I never did get past fifteen.

$comment: Hall 3, the apron: two small kin off the steps, the fight that exists to be won while the player is still dry. She stands at 13,19 watching row 19 across x9-12, and 9,19 and 10,19 are the only apron tiles that touch the south lane mouth, so she is unavoidable without standing in anybody's way. Measured, novice play, no items, 400 runs: lone starter at the solo-lead level 100/100/100, matched party at the team-raiser level 100/100/100.
name: Ollen
intro: You came down the steps walking. Everyone gets that bit right.
Let us see how you manage the part with no steps in it.
defeat: Fair enough. Go on and get in the water.
victory: Steps are behind you. Nothing down here is in any hurry.
afterward: Only one lane leaves this apron and it is not a choice. That is deliberate.

$comment: Hall 3, the west staithe -- what the lane washes in. THE SILTHOPPER IS THE REASON THIS ROW IS FAIR, and it is not decoration. A Tide Hall hits a Flame starter for double and takes half back from it, so every all-Tide lineup measured in the teens for Cinderpaw; Silthopper is terra/chitin, the one thing on this coast that BOTH Flame and Tide hit for double, and its moves are cut back to Quickstep and Nibble so it does not turn round and hit Verdant for double with Chitin. The first build of this row (Gullswift, Silthopper, Currentail) read 23 percent for Cinderpaw on the lone-starter column; a second with Anchorling in it read 21, because def 104 against a novice pressing one move is a wall rather than a fight. Measured, 400 runs: lone 100/97/100, matched 100/100/100.
name: Brae
intro: Nobody arrives at this staithe on purpose. The lane arrives here.
You are just what was in it.
defeat: Right. Race is off the east side. Have a look at where it is pointed.
victory: Drain is in the corner. It is not a punishment, it is a door.
afterward: Race leaves off the far side, one tile of it. You will know it when it has you.

$comment: Hall 3, the gate-hand, and the hardest of the three. NO "afterward" LINE, DELIBERATELY: her NPC carries both a trainer and the tg_winch script, and overworld interact answers with the trainer's afterward and returns before it ever reaches the script -- an afterward here would make the north sluice unturnable and the Hall unfinishable. Clatterclaw is capped to Closing Hold: with Shellstrike (chitin 65 off atk 104) the same row read 24 percent for Sprigling and 32 for Rilltail, because Chitin hits Verdant for double and both Tide starters bounce off a tide/chitin wall. Measured, 400 runs: lone 96/99/98, matched 100/100/100.
name: Nell
intro: Dead end, this staithe. I work the beam, so I am the only one meant to be standing on it.
You are going to want something off me shortly. Earn it first.
defeat: Hah. All right. Ask me about the sluice.
victory: Take the drain and come back when the water has stopped surprising you.

$comment: HALL 3, THE TIDE CREST, and the Tide Hall of Tideglass. Her party is the tank's own population -- a barnacle crab, a silt hopper, a gull and the race itself -- which is the flavour and the tuning at once, because it is deliberately not four Tide kin. The problem this row solves is the one Roxen solves with the type chart reversed: Tide hits Flame for double and Flame hits Tide for half, so a Cinderpaw player faces a Hall that punishes them on both sides of every exchange, and every all-Tide build measured between 0 and 13 percent for Cinderpaw. So the offence is spread: Pinchel swings Spray and Nibble, Silthopper swings Beast and Chitin, Gullswift is capped at 40-60 power, and only the ace is a real Tide attacker -- with flat-zero IVs and its two weakest moves. No bag item: Battle.doItem never consumes a foe-side item, so one Potion in that list is an unlimited heal rather than a Potion (see Roxen and Mabry). DO NOT RAISE THE LEVELS. Sixteen-to-nineteen was tried as eighteen-to-twenty-one and it bought two points on the matched row while dropping Cinderpaw from 81 to 35 on the lone row -- Currentail at 21 crosses a one-shot threshold against Blazelynx and the fight stops existing. Measured, novice play, no items, 400 runs: lone starter at the solo-lead level 96/81/100, matched party at the team-raiser level 100/100/100. The 81 is a lone Blazelynx walking a four-kin Keeper with no healing, which is the harness floor rather than a fight anybody has; the Hall 3 keeper this replaces read 0 percent there.
name: Marit Vane
intro: Right then. Water first and questions afterwards.
defeat: Huh.
victory: Out you go and get dry, and then come back and do it again.
Nobody in this city has ever got it right first time. Including me.
afterward: Go and listen to him. Then ask him what he does the first time the sea says no.

name: Wenna
intro: Morning. Mind the ropes and stay off the pad while the winch is running.
You are welcome to walk through. Everyone is. It is a public road and we did not forget that.
defeat: Well fought. Genuinely.
Take the incline slowly, it is steeper than it looks with a load on.
victory: No harm done. Sit down a minute, there is tea in the hut.
afterward: Forty crates and a crane, over a ridge, because a rock came down thirty-one years ago.
If you want to know what the Foundation actually does, it is mostly this. Moving things badly.
$comment: The first Meridian person the player fights, and she has to be LIKEABLE. She apologises for the road being full, she does not tell them to go around, and she offers them tea afterwards. Act 4 comes back to her: she genuinely does not know.

name: Kessel
intro: Careful up here. Wind takes people off this crest about once a decade.
Wind, and the fact that they were looking at the birds instead of their feet.
defeat: Fair. They fly better than they fight, and I have never minded that.
victory: Watch the wing on your left. Always the left, in an east wind.
afterward: Gullswift on the crest, three days running. Sea birds. Eleven miles inland and four hundred feet up.
I have wardened this ridge nineteen years and I have never had to write that down before.
$comment: The route's Gale trainer, and the one who tells the player what the encounter table is doing: a sea bird inland is the first quiet sign that something is wrong with the water, three maps before anybody says so.

name: Marrin
intro: Down and back, down and back. Sixteen days now.
Best wage I have ever earned and I have not once been told what is in the boxes.
defeat: Ha! Right. I needed that. Sixteen days of walking and no arguing at all.
victory: Board, lodging, a coat and a wage. You would take it too.
afterward: The card in Stonewake said no experience required. It meant it, and all.
Nine of us signed. Six were quarry lads. We none of us ask anything, and the wage comes on time.
$comment: The other end of the recruiting card on the wall of the Stonewake Meridian office. He is not a villain, he is a man with a job, and he is the reason the Order works: most of the Foundation is Marrin.
